entries.title: Job 3:1
segments: His day; the day of his birth, feeling that he had been deprived of all his possessions and of all capacity to enjoy life, and that thus existence had become a heavy calamity to him.  The language of Job throughout this chapter is that of passionate complaint against God's providence, and in using it he sinned; but Satan could not prevail with him to curse his Maker.

entries.title: Job 3:3
segments: A good man under trials may become fretful and peevish, have hard thoughts of God and his ways, and may say things which he will afterwards see to be foolish and wicked, and of which he will be utterly ashamed.

entries.title: Job 3:8
segments: Them--that curse the day; magicians, who were supposed to have power to curse certain days, as well as persons.  Compare what Balak says to Balaam,

. 
 
  To raise up their mourning; or, to raise up leviathan.  He would have the most powerful enchanters employed, who, according to the superstitious belief of the multitude, were able to raise up leviathan from the deep.

entries.title: Job 3:11
segments: Men if left to themselves under trials, may wish that they were dead, and be tempted sometimes even to kill themselves; but this is rebellion against God, and is the way to increase their own sorrows.

entries.title: Job 3:12
segments: Prevent me; in the old English sense of anticipating, being ready beforehand to meet one.

entries.title: Job 3:14
segments: Desolate places for themselves; cities in the desert; or perhaps sepulchres, which they built where they might rest and be quiet.  Had he died at his birth, Job thought he should have rested with equal quietness.

entries.title: Job 3:19
segments: There; in the grave, which Job here regards as a place of rest from the sufferings of life.

entries.title: Job 3:20
segments: Unto the bitter in soul; to him who pines in misery.

entries.title: Job 3:21
segments: Dig for it; earnestly desire and seek it.

entries.title: Job 3:23
segments:
Whose way is hid; so that he can see no possibility of escape from his sufferings. 
 
  Hedged in; so that he is shut up to calamity, without the hope of release. 
 
Men sometimes wonder why it is that God preserves their lives, when they seem to be receiving no good themselves, and doing no good to others.  But God has wise and good reasons; and through their preservation and trials, may bless not only them, but multitudes of others to the end of time and to eternity.

entries.title: Job 3:25
segments: The thing which I greatly feared is come upon me; or, "When I fear a fear, it comes upon me:" calamities more and more dreadful follow each other in quick succession.
